source.value: Suppose that $f(x,y)=x(y+1).$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)\ge 0?$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: q-121090

source.question: q-121090
source.value:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=0$ and $y=-1.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below. Since we have an "or equal to" inequality, we use solid lines to divide the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/599d3a551a20e68989e5de517711ae4c7c73255fb4a9d716797cf90dbb32a4ea.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/43bb5eac3414291bbd844a3608835a6f7be3e5e0dfcc2ae89426581eccdc87b3.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $x$ | $(y+1)$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(-1,0)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Top-Right | $(1,0)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-1,-2)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(1,-2)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |

 

Finally, on our diagram, we shade in the solutions to $f(x,y)\ge 0$ using the *last* column of the table above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/18757d46e86eb0d771841e7f5fe13be9ad464ccaf66b7190e7a2a7f02428a88e.png)
